title: problemsTableFrom
description: `problemsTableFrom` builds the read model's table on each read from the checks' run the query runner was given (`ReadView.checked`: the problems `runChecks` found after the load) and the product and domain rows, placing each problem's record in its product up its parents or by its ID; nothing keeps the table between reads. It is the only code that reads the run and the rows for the query and the only code that writes the table.

title: checkTableFrom
description: `checkTableFrom` builds the read model's table from the rows on each read: each source table is read once, and nothing keeps the table between reads. It is the only code that reads the source rows for the queries and the only code that writes the table.

title: limitsTableFrom
description: `limitsTableFrom` builds the read model's table from the rows on each read: each source table is read once, and nothing keeps the table between reads. It is the only code that reads the source rows for the queries and the only code that writes the table.

title: essentialReviewTableFrom
description: `essentialReviewTableFrom` builds the read model's table from the rows on each read, reading which records are essential and which kinds are read as accidental-in-essential reads them (`essential.ts`); nothing keeps the table between reads. It is the only code that reads the source rows for the query and the only code that writes the table.

title: recordSummariesTableFrom
description: `recordSummariesTableFrom` builds the table from the rows on each read: every record as `placementOf` places it (up its parents, by its ID's product or domain, or in the one domain that uses it; the placement the store keeps for every projection that reads it), each kind's rows read once with their part rows and the links they start for the digest (kept while those rows are the same), sorted by the shared ID order, then each product's space. It is the only code that reads the rows for the query and the only code that writes the table.

title: folderTreeTableFrom
description: `folderTreeTableFrom` builds every product's tree from the rows on each read: the records placed by `placeRecords`, each record's folded children of its own stage, kind by kind in the schema's order (capabilities and flow steps by position and path, terms bottom-up), Shared and each domain's stages with a folder per kind that can start a branch there. It is the only code that reads the rows for the query and the only code that writes the table.

title: layOut
description: `layOut` lays out the map of an input (its view, Tree, Nested or Map, and its root's tree from the folder tree) with placeTree, placeNested or placeGround in the layout's worker, or on the page's thread where there is none, only when the packed input changed: the layouts made lately are kept in memory by their input, and each product's Map last shown keeps its boxes in the next one until Tidy up.

title: erdTableFrom
description: `erdTableFrom` builds each product's map from the rows on each read: its domains, their aggregates and entities (the root first) with their fields, and the has_one and has_many links and the fields typed by another aggregate as lines. It is the only code that reads the rows for the query and the only code that writes the table.

title: recordHistory
description: recordHistory: the commits that changed the record's rows, read from git's log and diffs on each request (parseLog, changesInDiff).

title: spaceOf
description: `useSpaceState` maps the products of each loaded index, in ID order, through `spaceOf`: the product's `icon` field when `iconField` accepts it, else its ID's monogram, and its `color` field when `colorField` accepts it, else a color derived from its ID. It is worked out again only when a load gives a new index.

title: recordChangesTableFrom
description: `recordChangesTableFrom` builds the table on each read from the rows now and the baseline the server read from git for the query's `since`, comparing them by record (`recordChanges`) and keeping each product's own. It is the only code that reads them for the query and the only code that writes the table.

title: viewTableFrom
description: `viewTableFrom` builds the read model's table from the View aggregate's tables and every record's ID, on each read: each source table is read once and indexed, and nothing keeps the table between reads. It is the only code that reads the source rows for the queries and the only code that writes the table.

title: endpointTableFrom
description: `endpointTableFrom` builds the read model's table from the Endpoint aggregate's tables, the commands and queries, the domains and every record's ID, on each read: each source table is read once and indexed, and nothing keeps the table between reads. It is the only code that reads the source rows for the queries and the only code that writes the table.

title: integrationTableFrom
description: `integrationTableFrom` builds the read model's table from the Integration aggregate's tables, the products and every record's ID, on each read: each source table is read once and indexed, and nothing keeps the table between reads. It is the only code that reads the source rows for the queries and the only code that writes the table.

title: uiComponentTableFrom
description: `uiComponentTableFrom` builds the read model's table from the UI component aggregate's tables and every record's ID, on each read: each source table is read once and indexed, and nothing keeps the table between reads. It is the only code that reads the source rows for the queries and the only code that writes the table.

title: domainTableFrom
description: `domainTableFrom` builds the read model's table from the Domain aggregate's tables and every record's ID, on each read: each source table is read once and indexed, and nothing keeps the table between reads. It is the only code that reads the source rows for the queries and the only code that writes the table. It lists each domain's terms bottom-up with `termsBottomUp`, the one order every glossary uses (the app's nav and wiki included).

title: specificationTableFrom
description: `specificationTableFrom` builds the read model's table from the Specification aggregate's tables and every record's ID, on each read: each source table is read once and indexed, and nothing keeps the table between reads. It is the only code that reads the source rows for the queries and the only code that writes the table.

title: aggregateTableFrom
description: `aggregateTableFrom` builds the read model's table from the Aggregate aggregate's tables, the commands, tables and domain events under it, the links that raise and hear its events, and every record's ID, on each read: each source table is read once and indexed, and nothing keeps the table between reads. It is the only code that reads the source rows for the queries and the only code that writes the table.

title: domainEventTableFrom
description: `domainEventTableFrom` builds the read model's table from the Domain event aggregate's tables, the links that raise and hear each event, the aggregates and every record's ID, on each read: each source table is read once and indexed, and nothing keeps the table between reads. It is the only code that reads the source rows for the queries and the only code that writes the table.

title: commandTableFrom
description: `commandTableFrom` builds the read model's table from the Command aggregate's tables, the endpoints that expose each command, the entities and aggregates they sit in, and every record's ID, on each read: each source table is read once and indexed, and nothing keeps the table between reads. It is the only code that reads the source rows for the queries and the only code that writes the table.

title: valueObjectTableFrom
description: `valueObjectTableFrom` builds the read model's table from the Value object aggregate's tables and every record's ID, on each read: each source table is read once and indexed, and nothing keeps the table between reads. It is the only code that reads the source rows for the queries and the only code that writes the table.

title: readModelTableFrom
description: `readModelTableFrom` builds the read model's table from the Read model aggregate's tables and every record's ID, on each read: each source table is read once and indexed, and nothing keeps the table between reads. It is the only code that reads the source rows for the queries and the only code that writes the table.

title: storageRequirementTableFrom
description: `storageRequirementTableFrom` builds the read model's table from the aggregate's tables, what names it and every record's ID, on each read: each source table is read once and indexed, and nothing keeps the table between reads. It is the only code that reads the source rows for the queries and the only code that writes the table.

title: readWorkspace
description: `readWorkspace`, filled from a store whose data is built whole: `loadWorkspace` opens a store afresh, and the server runs it in the background on its kept store's data built whole (`Store.whole`) after each burst of changes. It gives each record its part rows (`readRecords`), fills the file facts, runs Lathe's checks then the product's on four connections and the coverage queries side by side; `buildReference`'s answer is kept until the files change. Its shape is `Workspace` in lathe/src/types.ts.

title: keymapTableFrom
description: `resolveCommands` and `platformKeys`: the keymap's commands with the person's changed shortcuts in their place, each with its defaults and whether it changed or may, worked out again on each change of the Key bindings.

title: themesTableFrom
description: The built-in themes and the person's own (`themes`), with the one in use (`active`) and the color mode, worked out again from the person's appearance on each change.

title: recentFoldersTableFrom
description: `menuTemplate`'s Open Recent items: each recent folder, latest first, shown with `displayPath`, from the list the shell keeps in memory (read from recent-folders.json as it starts); the menu is rebuilt whenever the list changes.

title: listSessions
description: Reads Claude Code's own session store, one transcript per session under `~/.claude/projects/<folder>/`, and never writes it: each transcript's first and last 64 KB for its title, and the registry of running sessions (`~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json`) for those open elsewhere, each time the picker asks.

title: useViewState
description: The focus page registers a reader of what it shows (its focus, stage, selection and wiki card) while it is mounted, and the app bridge's question calls it, so nothing is kept between questions.

title: chatPatch
description: Writes the chat as the patch from what the page last had: the whole chat when it had none, else only the items that changed.

title: metaModelTableFrom
description: `metaModelTableFrom` builds the read model's table from the schema on each read: the kinds sorted by position then name, the stages by position, each relation's pairs, and every non-link table's columns. It is the only code that reads the schema for the query and the only code that writes the table.

title: listSkills
description: Reads each skill's SKILL.md and each command's file for its frontmatter, from the folder, the Owner's Claude folder, the installed plugins and the Lathe plugin, each time the Owner starts a slash.

title: referenceOf
description: `referenceOf` fills it with every kind, table, relation, stage and check, from the store's schema, kind order and check rows. It is computed on request, and `buildReference` keeps the answer in `referenceCache` while no data file or migration changes.

title: recordDataFileTableFrom
description: `recordDataFileTableFrom` builds the table from the rows: each record's kind by its ID, every kind's rows read once, and the data folder of the store that holds them (`ReadView.dataDir`), none for data read from no one folder. The store keeps it until a table it read changes. It is the only code that reads the rows for the query and the only code that writes the table.

title: productTableFrom
description: `productTableFrom` builds the read model's table from the Product aggregate's tables, the business outcomes, domains, capabilities, use cases and flows of each product, and every record's ID, on each read; nothing keeps the table between reads. It is the only code that reads the source rows for the queries and the only code that writes the table.

title: businessOutcomeTableFrom
description: `businessOutcomeTableFrom` builds the read model's table from the business outcomes, their measured_by and serves links, and every record's ID, on each read; nothing keeps the table between reads. It is the only code that reads the source rows for the queries and the only code that writes the table.

title: extensionRecordTableFrom
description: `extensionRecordTableFrom` builds the read model's table from every product kind's table, the links each kind may start, the packages used, where every record sits and the products, on each read; nothing keeps the table between reads. It is the only code that reads the source rows for the queries and the only code that writes the table.

title: journeyTableFrom
description: `journeyTableFrom` builds the read model's table from the journeys, their steps and tests, the carries_out, serves and starts_from links, and the use cases, actors, capabilities, policies, events and commands the steps carry out, on each read; nothing keeps the table between reads. It is the only code that reads the source rows for the queries and the only code that writes the table.

title: standardTableFrom
description: `standardTableFrom` builds the read model's table from the Standard aggregate's tables and every record's ID, on each read: each source table is read once and indexed, and nothing keeps the table between reads. It is the only code that reads the source rows for the queries and the only code that writes the table.

title: tableTableFrom
description: `tableTableFrom` builds the read model's table from the Table aggregate's tables and every record's ID, on each read: each source table is read once and indexed, and nothing keeps the table between reads. It is the only code that reads the source rows for the queries and the only code that writes the table.

title: entryPointTableFrom
description: `entryPointTableFrom` builds the read model's table from the entry points, the packages they use, the standard rules they meet, and every record's ID, on each read; nothing keeps the table between reads. It is the only code that reads the source rows for the queries and the only code that writes the table.

title: toolingTableFrom
description: `toolingTableFrom` builds the read model's table from the tooling records, the packages they use, the standard rules they meet, and every record's ID, on each read; nothing keeps the table between reads. It is the only code that reads the source rows for the queries and the only code that writes the table.

title: dataStoreTableFrom
description: `dataStoreTableFrom` builds the read model's table from the aggregate's tables, what names it and every record's ID, on each read: each source table is read once and indexed, and nothing keeps the table between reads. It is the only code that reads the source rows for the queries and the only code that writes the table.

title: coverageTableFrom
description: `coverageTableFrom` builds the table on each read from the checks' run the query runner was given (`ReadView.checked`: the coverage `runChecks` worked out after the load), each product's scopes its own first. It is the only code that reads the run for the query and the only code that writes the table.

title: coverageGapsTableFrom
description: `coverageGapsTableFrom` builds the table on each read from the checks' run the query runner was given (`ReadView.checked`): each scope's `Coverage.gaps`, the product's own first. Those gaps are worked out once, on the load: `coverageViewsSql` (lathe/src/coverage.ts) recreates `coverage_gap` from `coverage_item`, the gap rules' minimums by record and the rules for source files, routes and packages (`PACKAGE_GAP_SQL` over the `package_facts` that `readPackageFacts` reads from the manifests), and `computeCoverage` reads it with `COVERAGE_GAPS_SQL`. It is the only code that reads the run for the queries and the only code that writes the table.

title: testsByStateTableFrom
description: `testsByStateTableFrom` builds the table on each read from the checks' run the query runner was given (`ReadView.checked`): each scope's `Coverage.tests`, the product's own first, then each domain by position. Those counts are worked out once, on the load: `coverageViewsSql` (lathe/src/coverage.ts) makes `coverage_tests` a view joining each scope to the tests of `test_run` and counting them by state, and `computeCoverage` reads it with `COVERAGE_TESTS_SQL`. It is the only code that reads the run for the query and the only code that writes the table.

title: owed_pattern_rules
description: `coverageViewsSql` recreates `owed_pattern_rules` as a table on every load: every rule of each pattern, in every domain that follows it, itself or through a use case.

title: fileFactsTableFrom
description: `fileFactsTableFrom` builds the table on each read from the checks' run the query runner was given (`ReadView.checked`): the endpoint-route-not-in-file and view-route-not-in-file problems on each product's records, and its route-without-record gaps. Those are worked out once, on the load: `gatherFileFacts` (lathe/src/index.ts) reads each file a record names into `file_facts`, `gatherRouteFacts` (lathe/src/trace/routes.ts) reads each endpoint's and view's address against the files of what implements it and the addresses the code serves into `route_facts` and `served_routes`, and the address checks and the gap rule read them. It is the only code that reads the run for the query and the only code that writes the table.

title: recordTraceTableFrom
description: `recordTraceTableFrom` works out a record's trace when it is asked for, from the rows and the checks' run the query runner was given (chains, coverage and problems): the records placed once, then by its kind's obligation flag, a use case's requirements or a test's run by. It is the only code that reads them for the query and the only code that writes the table.

title: storedRecordFactsTableFrom
description: `storedRecordFactsTableFrom` builds the table on each read from the checks' run the query runner was given (`ReadView.checked`): the table-schema-mismatch warnings on each product's records. Those are worked out once, on the load: `gatherTableFacts` (lathe/src/trace/tables.ts) reads, once per file, the file each table kept in a database names and makes one fact for the table, each column and each key, found or not, into `table_facts`, and the table-schema-mismatch check words one warning per part not found. It is the only code that reads the run for the query and the only code that writes the table.

title: followingTableFrom
description: `followingTableFrom` builds the read model's table from the rows on each read: each source table is read once, and nothing keeps the table between reads. It is the only code that reads the source rows for the queries and the only code that writes the table.

title: servesTableFrom
description: `servesTableFrom` works out the table from the rows on each read: the Serves reach (`servesOf`) once, each record placed once, every record's outcomes and each product's list. It is the only code that reads the rows for the queries and the only code that writes the table.

title: traceTableFrom
description: `traceTableFrom` builds the read model's table on each read from the rows (use cases, their requirements, flows and steps, and what those reach, placed in their products) and the checks' run the query runner was given (coverage's gaps and the chains' tests), with the Serves reach (`useCaseReaches`) for what each use case changes and reads.

title: changeReachTableFrom
description: `changeReachTableFrom` indexes, once per read, each record's dependents from the rows (its children, the records that name it through a link or a column of theirs or their parts) and the checks' chains (its build records and tests), then walks them breadth first from each changed record, leaving out the links up to a purpose. It is the only code that reads them for the query and the only code that writes the table.

title: testDataSetTableFrom
description: `testDataSetTableFrom` builds the read model's table from the Test data set aggregate's tables and every record's ID, on each read: each source table is read once and indexed, and nothing keeps the table between reads. It is the only code that reads the source rows for the queries and the only code that writes the table.

title: useCaseTableFrom
description: `useCaseTableFrom` builds the read model's table from the Use case aggregate's tables, the capabilities, interfaces and every record's ID, on each read: each source table is read once and indexed, and nothing keeps the table between reads. It is the only code that reads the source rows for the queries and the only code that writes the table.

title: patternTableFrom
description: `patternTableFrom` builds the read model's table from the Pattern aggregate's tables and every record's ID, on each read: each source table is read once and indexed, and nothing keeps the table between reads. It is the only code that reads the source rows for the queries and the only code that writes the table.
